note: One register per claim, so one build carries them all and each oracle filters to its own register. authority: a guarded name correction whose authority is the same native variable's edition 100, delivered by two physical rows, renames edition 99 and keeps all three originals. conflict: two entries give edition 99 different names; edition 100 already delivers 'Reviewed label', so if 'Reviewed label' won, edition 99 would agree with edition 100 and ANSWER would form states; withholding both leaves none, and the conflict issue names both entries. shared: the correction names FIRST, one of two literal columns of one record. period: ANSWER shares its edition-99 record with OTHER, so the period entry is overbroad and applies nowhere. sentinel/substantive: the scoped sentinel binds book FIX only where the source list's 99 is exactly 'Unknown' and keeps the source list. parallel: Sibling shares First's record but has its own partition owner; the parallel window still binds First and Second. par: the digest-guarded subset splits of ATC and KVA (each with two PAR_OV rows) carry their data warning on every routed state; DIA's period entry needs no native edition and gives PAR_OV DIA exactly 2011 and 2013 while PAR_SV keeps its delivered period. DIA's expected_fields, expected_scope and expected_period are written out because the placeholder selectors have no subset filter (variable:DIA matches both subsets); they copy the prepared PAR_OV record, as a placeholder would, including its unknown-scope label.
fails_if: authority: `compile_occurrence_corrections` checks the evidence digest over the target alone instead of the whole native family, so the digest over all three originals mismatches and the rename goes stale; conflict: `apply_occurrence_cases` keeps the first `[[errata.field]]` value instead of withholding competing values; shared: `compile_occurrence_corrections` targets every literal projection of the selected record, so SECOND is renamed too; period: `compile_occurrence_corrections` accepts a period entry on a record that projects a second literal column; sentinel: `compile_coding_register` matches sentinel members by code alone, so 'Substantive industry' also binds FIX; parallel: `compile_parallel_representations` matches its owner against native variables instead of partition-corrected owners, so the entry goes stale; par: `compile_partitions` drops a guarded split's `data_warning`, or the SOS `[[errata.occurrence_period]]` is refused without a native edition
